Subject: POC scope & risk triage — AtlasHealth trial

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed baseline for the POC and a mitigation path for risks you raised.

Recap / success criteria (please confirm or edit):
- Throughput: support 150 concurrent inference requests at median latency < 250ms (95th < 450ms) for the clinical summary model.
- Accuracy: match AtlasHealth baseline on the benchmark prompt set with F1 >= 0.82 for entity extraction and no high-severity hallucinations on a 50-case sample.
- Security: deployment in our Dedicated sandbox with encrypted-at-rest keys; evidence to satisfy your security intake (SOC2 report + SSO configuration).
- Integration: end-to-end test with your sample payloads and the ingestion pipeline (daily batch + on-demand).

Timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (now): exchange access + sample payloads, SOC2 + SSO details.
- Week 1: environment provisioning, initial ingestion test, run smoke checks.
- Week 2: focused perf tuning and mapping adapter; iterate on failures found.
- Week 3: run benchmark evaluation, produce pass/fail report and next-step recommendations.

Immediate risks we flagged on the call:
1) Data mapping mismatch between Atlas schema and Redwood tokenizer -> may cause tokenization/parse errors.
2) Security evidence / SSO details required by Atlas security team before production-like access.
3) Potential edge-case causing higher latency on 4k+ token inputs.

Mitigations proposed:
- Redwood will provide a mapping adapter + pre-parse transform to normalize payloads (Aditya to own).
- I will share Redwood’s SOC2 report and the SSO integration guide (see links below).
- We’ll run a targeted perf test against long context inputs and set a fallback model if 95th pct latency exceeds SLA.

Action items / owners:
- Atlas: confirm success criteria and nominate POC owner + tech lead (Sam).
- Atlas: provide 3 representative sample payloads and any ingestion docs by EOD Mon.
- Redwood: share SOC2 and SSO docs (Marissa) and deliver mapping adapter prototype (Aditya) within 48-72 hours of sample payloads.
- Schedule: propose a 30-min sync next Tuesday to review the first ingestion run.

Attachments: [Attachment: poc-checklist.xlsx (18KB)]

Thanks — aiming to keep this tight so your evaluation can be decisive.

— Marissa

Hi all — I started a triage on the sample schema Priya dropped in the share (thanks). Early findings:

1) Root cause (repro): several fields in the payload are JSON-encoded strings that contain escaped newlines and nested JSON (e.g., clinical_notes field stored as a string). Our tokenizer expects raw text, so the current ingestion path performs a string->json decode at parse time which can lead to tokenization boundary mismatches and occasional parse exceptions. Repro steps: take sample_02.json -> run ingestion -> see tokenization error stack (snippet below).

Stack snippet (sanitized):
- com.redwood.ingest.TokenizerException: unexpected token at pos 482
- at com.redwood.tokenize.Tokenizer.parse(Tokenizer.java:214)
- at com.redwood.ingest.PayloadParser.normalize(PayloadParser.java:88)

2) Impact: this can cause failed inference requests (5-7% of test items) and intermittent higher latency while the parser retries. This is a blocking issue for a clean baseline evaluation.

3) Proposed mitigation (short-term): introduce a pre-parse transform that detects JSON-in-strings and normalizes clinical_notes to raw text. This is a low-risk change we can ship as a patch to the ingestion service and enable per-tenant. Estimate: 48 hours to deliver, followed by a canary to your sandbox.

Attachments: [Attachment: error-log.txt (6KB)]

Request: Sam/Priya — can you confirm where clinical_notes is sourced (EHR export / ETL) and share 1-2 larger examples (~5-10KB) so we can validate the transform on realistic inputs?

I’ll open an internal ticket and link it here once created.

— Aditya
